description:
FOUND s508 (Fable, 2026-10-05) by the review probes for s507c PART ONE.  (a) and (c) are PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466; (b) became visible with s507c's #2690 (before it `pcl -c` said "syntax OK" and never reached the failing `use`).

REPRODUCERS (probe names in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s508/review/ph.pl (IMPL TAG [REGEX]; answers in out/ph.perl / ph.base / ph.tree; perl 5.40.3, main fee16466, the s507c tree 0229e0ec)):
 (a) c-late-use     pcl -c p.pl   with  CHECK { print "chk\n" } use List::Util; use NoSuch::Mod; print "run\n";
                    perl: chk on STDOUT, then "Can't locate NoSuch/Mod.pm ... BEGIN failed", status 2      s507c tree: no `chk` (the message and the status are right)
     mod-die-use    use lib "."; CHECK { print "c\n" } use D; print "run\n";   with D.pm = package D; CHECK { print "D:c\n" } INIT {..} die "D died\n"; 1;
                    perl: D:c / c on STDOUT, then the error, status 255          tree: nothing on STDOUT
     ph-exit-begin  ... BEGIN { print "b\n"; exit 4 } ...  is ALREADY right on the tree (b / c / end, status 4).
     perl's rule (perl.c, perl_parse): when the parse is left by my_exit / a compile-time die, the UNITCHECK and CHECK queues are still called.
 (b) c-file-use-lib pcl -c p.pl   with  use lib '.'; use M; use NoSuch::Mod2;   (M.pm has BEGIN / CHECK / INIT / UNITCHECK / END blocks and a printing body)
                    perl: M:begin / M:unitcheck / M:body / M:check, then the error, status 2
                    tree: M:begin / M:unitcheck / M:body / M:end, then the error, status 2      -- an END block ran under -c (perl -c never runs END or INIT), and M:check did not (= (a))
 (c) c-check-exit   pcl -c -e 'CHECK { print "c\n"; exit 5 } print "run\n"'
                    perl: c, status 5, NO "syntax OK"          main and tree: c, "-e syntax OK" on STDERR, status 0
     (without -c the same program is right: probe ph-exit-check, status 3.)

THE OTHER HALF OF (a), a module that dies under eval at BEGIN time:
     mod-die-eval   use lib "."; BEGIN { eval { require D }; print "caught: $@" } CHECK { print "c\n" } INIT { print "i\n" } print "run\n";
                    perl: caught: D died / c / D:c / D:i / i / run      tree: caught: D died / c / i / run   (the blocks D compiled before it died are dropped by %p-load-unit's non-local exit; perl keeps them queued)
     -- this one is in s507c's resume brief (s508) as a small review finding; the rest of this task is not.

SIZE: small; one place each -- the compile-phase runner's abnormal exit, the exit path's "are we under -c" test, and how -c's own CHECK block meets a user exit.  Exit STATUS differences of a die after a `use` are #2740, not this.


=== s507c (s509): NOT done ===
Not started in s507c (PART TWO shipped #2700 #2701 #2703 #2666 #2669 #2689 #2761 only).  For #2763 the s508 reading stands: emulating -c CHECK by draining queued blocks on an abnormal compile end would print "syntax OK" from the drain, so it needs a design of where -c's verdict is printed relative to the drain.
subject: When the compile phase ends abnormally: perl still runs the queued UNITCHECK and CHECK blocks when a BEGIN / `use` DIES (PCL: only when BEGIN calls exit); under `pcl -c` a failed compile runs END blocks (perl -c: never) and a user CHECK block's `exit N` is swallowed ("syntax OK", status 0)
